questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How the first vaccines were invented and tested
Why the Black Death was worse than Covid-19
How rich countries can help poorer countries
The different ways pandemics come to an end
questions.why: Neil says they'll be finding out how pandemics end, and experts discuss biological and social endings.

questions.q: What does Sam say about the Black Death in the Middle Ages?
options: It was ended quickly by the first vaccines
It killed over half of Europe in four years
It only affected a few cities in Europe
It lasted for more than a hundred years
questions.why: Sam says the Black Death killed over half of Europe's population and lasted for four years.

questions.q: According to Neil, how do most people feel about Covid now?
options: Tired of worrying and keen for normal life
Happy to keep all the lockdown rules for years
More frightened of Covid than ever before
Not interested in the news about new variants
questions.why: Neil says most people are sick of worrying about Covid and can't wait for things to get back to normal.

questions.q: According to Professor Nicholas Christakis, how do pandemics end socially?
options: When scientists find a cure for the disease
When the government closes all the borders
When people agree it's over and take more risk
When nobody in the world is sick any more
questions.why: He says they end socially when everyone agrees they've ended and is willing to tolerate more risk.

questions.q: What does Professor Christakis suggest about declaring a pandemic over?
options: We might do it too early and ignore the truth
We should always wait for the WHO to decide
It only happens after a disease is eradicated
It is always the right decision for society
questions.why: He says we declare victory 'maybe prematurely', or 'we put our heads in the sand'.

questions.q: Which countries does Sam say are in a better position than most?
options: Countries that had very strict lockdowns
Countries with very small populations
Countries that closed their borders early
Rich western countries able to vaccinate
questions.why: Sam says rich western countries with the resources to vaccinate their populations are better placed.

questions.q: What does Professor Dora Vargha say happened with HIV/Aids?
options: Scientists found a cure for it in the 1980s
It became a long-term, manageable illness
It stopped being a problem in every country
It became much more deadly over time
questions.why: She says it went from 'an immediate death sentence' to 'a manageable chronic disease' where medicine is available.

questions.q: What are many scientists warning about Covid, according to Sam?
options: The pandemic will certainly end next year
Vaccines no longer protect people from it
We're not yet at the beginning of the end
Covid is now more dangerous than HIV/Aids
questions.why: Sam says scientists warn we haven't yet reached the beginning of the end, but maybe the end of the beginning.
